jp: 駅[えき]に{着[つ]いたら|cd-tara}、電話[でんわ]してください。
en: When you get to the station, please call me.
why: A request that follows a completed action is the core job of たら; と and なら cannot lead into a request here.

jp: 仕事[しごと]が{終[お]わったら|cd-tara}、一緒[いっしょ]に晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べましょう。
en: Once work is over, let's have dinner together.
why: An invitation after something finishes takes たら; と cannot lead into an invitation, and なら would not mean 'once it is over'.

jp: 大人[おとな]に{なったら|cd-tara}、医者[いしゃ]になりたいです。
en: When I grow up, I want to become a doctor.
why: A wish for after a change of state is stated with たら; と cannot lead into a wish.

jp: 日本[にほん]に{行[い]ったら|cd-tara}、まず京都[きょうと]を見[み]たいです。
en: When I get to Japan, I want to see Kyoto first.
why: 'Once I am there' plus a wish is たら; と cannot lead into a wish, ても means 'even if' and ので gives a reason, not a time.

jp: 家[いえ]に{帰[かえ]ったら/帰[かえ]ると|cd-tara}、玄関[げんかん]に荷物[にもつ]が置[お]いてありました。
en: When I got home, a package had been left at the entrance.
why: Discovering something after doing an action in the past is たら (or と); ば and なら cannot describe a single past event.

jp: 朝[あさ]{起[お]きたら/起[お]きると|cd-tara}、窓[まど]の外[そと]が真[ま]っ白[しろ]でした。
en: When I woke up in the morning, it was all white outside the window.
why: A past discovery ('I did X and found Y') takes たら or と; ば, なら and ても do not fit a past event.

jp: 窓[まど]を{開[あ]けたら/開[あ]けると|cd-tara}、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っていました。
en: When I opened the window, it was snowing.
why: Opening something and discovering what is there is たら (or と); ば and なら cannot report a one-off past discovery.

jp: 部屋[へや]に{入[はい]ったら/入[はい]ると|cd-tara}、誰[だれ]もいませんでした。
en: When I went into the room, nobody was there.
why: Entering and finding something is a past discovery, which takes たら or と.

jp: 友達[ともだち]に{電話[でんわ]したら/電話[でんわ]すると|cd-tara}、まだ寝[ね]ていました。
en: When I called my friend, he was still asleep.
why: 'I did X and found Y' in the past takes たら or と; ば and なら do not report what actually happened.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]を{見[み]たら/見[み]ると|cd-tara}、牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]がありませんでした。
en: When I looked in the fridge, there was no milk.
why: Looking and finding the result is a past discovery, so たら (or と) is needed.

jp: 辞書[じしょ]で{調[しら]べたら/調[しら]べると|cd-tara}、意味[いみ]がすぐわかりました。
en: When I looked it up in the dictionary, I understood the meaning right away.
why: The action led to a result that actually happened in the past, which is たら or と.

jp: 試[ため]しに{食[た]べてみたら/食[た]べてみると|cd-tara}、思[おも]ったよりおいしかったです。
en: When I tried eating it, it was tastier than I had expected.
why: Trying something and finding out how it was is a past discovery: たら or と.

jp: 新[あたら]しい靴[くつ]を{履[は]いたら/履[は]くと|cd-tara}、足[あし]が痛[いた]くなりました。
en: When I put on my new shoes, my feet began to hurt.
why: One concrete past event followed by its result takes たら or と; ば and なら do not fit.

jp: 部屋[へや]を{掃除[そうじ]したら/掃除[そうじ]すると|cd-tara}、古[ふる]い写真[しゃしん]が出[で]てきました。
en: When I cleaned the room, an old photo turned up.
why: Cleaning led to an unexpected finding in the past, which is たら or と.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に{聞[き]いたら/聞[き]くと|cd-tara}、「いいですよ」と言[い]われました。
en: When I asked my teacher, I was told, "That's fine."
why: A one-off past action and the answer it brought is たら or と; ば and なら do not fit.

jp: 春[はる]に{なったら|cd-tara}、花見[はなみ]に行[い]きましょう。
en: When spring comes, let's go to see the cherry blossoms.
why: An invitation tied to a future moment takes たら; と cannot be followed by an invitation.

jp: 十時[じゅうじ]に{なったら|cd-tara}、起[お]こしてください。
en: When it gets to ten o'clock, please wake me up.
why: A request to act when a point in time arrives uses たら; と cannot lead into a request.

jp: 熱[ねつ]が{下[さ]がったら|cd-tara}、学校[がっこう]に行[い]ってもいいですよ。
en: Once your fever goes down, you may go to school.
why: Permission that depends on something being completed takes たら; と does not lead into permission.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]が{終[お]わったら|cd-tara}、ゲームをしてもいいです。
en: Once your homework is done, you may play games.
why: 'After X is done, you may Y' is the standard たら pattern; と cannot lead into permission.

jp: 大学[だいがく]を{卒業[そつぎょう]したら|cd-tara}、国[くに]へ帰[かえ]るつもりです。
en: After I graduate from university, I intend to go back to my country.
d: 卒業[そつぎょう]すると
卒業[そつぎょう]するなら
卒業[そつぎょう]しても
why: An intention that comes after a completed step takes たら; と cannot lead into an intention.

jp: 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を{食[た]べたら|cd-tara}、散歩[さんぽ]しませんか。
en: After we eat lunch, shall we take a walk?
why: An invitation after finishing an action takes たら; と cannot lead into an invitation.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]を{買[か]ったら|cd-tara}、ホームで待[ま]っていてください。
en: After you buy your ticket, please wait on the platform.
why: A request that follows a completed action takes たら; と cannot lead into a request.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]が{届[とど]いたら|cd-tara}、すぐにお知[し]らせしますね。
en: Once the package arrives, I'll let you know right away.
why: A promise to act once something happens takes たら; と cannot lead into a promise, and なら would not mean 'once it arrives'.

jp: 準備[じゅんび]が{できたら|cd-tara}、呼[よ]んでください。
en: When you're ready, please call me.
why: A request that depends on something being completed takes たら; と cannot lead into a request.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]が{始[はじ]まったら|cd-tara}、携帯[けいたい]の電源[でんげん]を切[き]ってください。
en: Once the meeting starts, please turn off your mobile phone.
why: A request that applies once something has begun takes たら; と cannot lead into a request.

jp: お金[かね]が{貯[た]まったら|cd-tara}、新[あたら]しいパソコンを買[か]います。
en: Once I have saved enough money, I will buy a new computer.
why: A plan that follows a completed step takes たら; と cannot lead into a plan of one's own.

jp: 大学[だいがく]に{入[はい]ったら|cd-tara}、一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしを始[はじ]めるつもりです。
en: Once I get into university, I plan to start living on my own.
why: An intention that follows a future event takes たら; と cannot lead into an intention.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は子[こ]どもが{寝[ね]たら|cd-tara}、ゆっくり映画[えいが]を見[み]ようと思[おも]います。
en: Tonight, once the children are asleep, I'm going to watch a film in peace.
why: The speaker's own plan after a future event takes たら; と cannot lead into the speaker's will.

jp: 病気[びょうき]が{治[なお]ったら|cd-tara}、また働[はたら]きます。
en: When I have recovered from my illness, I will work again.
why: The speaker's own plan after recovery takes たら; と cannot lead into the speaker's will.

jp: 雨[あめ]が{止[や]んだら|cd-tara}、出[で]かけましょう。
en: When the rain stops, let's go out.
why: An invitation tied to the rain stopping takes たら; と cannot lead into an invitation.

jp: 雪[ゆき]が{降[ふ]ったら/降[ふ]れば|cd-tara}、スキーに行[い]こう。
en: If it snows, let's go skiing.
why: A suggestion about what to do if something happens takes たら (ば also works); と cannot lead into 'let's' and ので states a fact, not an 'if'.

jp: 時間[じかん]が{できたら|cd-tara}、連絡[れんらく]します。
en: When I have some time, I will get in touch.
why: A promise that depends on an event takes たら; と cannot lead into a promise, ても means 'even if' and ので gives a reason.

jp: もし宝[たから]くじが{当[あ]たったら/当[あ]たれば|cd-tara}、世界[せかい]を旅行[りょこう]したいです。
en: If I won the lottery, I would like to travel around the world.
why: A wish about an imagined event uses たら (ば is also fine); と cannot lead into a wish and ても would mean 'even if'.

jp: もっと早[はや]く家[いえ]を{出[で]ていたら/出[で]ていれば|cd-tara}、電車[でんしゃ]に間[ま]に合[あ]ったのに。
en: If I had left home earlier, I would have caught the train.
why: A counterfactual about the past takes 〜ていたら (or 〜ていれば); と and なら cannot express it.

jp: 傘[かさ]を{持[も]って来[き]ていたら/持[も]って来[き]ていれば|cd-tara}、濡[ぬ]れなかったのに。
en: If I had brought an umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten wet.
why: A past counterfactual takes 〜ていたら (or 〜ていれば); と and なら do not work, and ても changes it to 'even if'.

jp: あの時[とき]もっと{勉強[べんきょう]していたら/勉強[べんきょう]していれば|cd-tara}、合格[ごうかく]できたかもしれません。
en: If I had studied harder back then, I might have passed.
d: 勉強[べんきょう]すると
勉強[べんきょう]するなら
勉強[べんきょう]しても
why: Regret about an unreal past takes 〜ていたら (or 〜ていれば); と and なら cannot express it.

jp: 若[わか]い時[とき]に{留学[りゅうがく]していたら/留学[りゅうがく]していれば|cd-tara}、今[いま]は英語[えいご]が話[はな]せたのに。
en: If I had studied abroad when I was young, I could speak English now.
d: 留学[りゅうがく]すると
留学[りゅうがく]するなら
留学[りゅうがく]しても
why: A counterfactual about the past takes 〜ていたら (or 〜ていれば); と and なら do not fit.

jp: 病院[びょういん]に{行[い]ったら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: Why don't you go to the hospital?
why: A suggestion is made with 〜たらどうですか; the other forms cannot be followed by どうですか in this sense.

jp: 少[すこ]し{休[やす]んだら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: Why don't you rest for a while?
why: Gentle advice is formed with 〜たらどうですか; no other form can sit in front of どうですか here.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に{相談[そうだん]したら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: Why don't you talk it over with your teacher?
d: 相談[そうだん]するので
why: Advice is expressed as 〜たらどうですか; the other forms do not make a suggestion.

jp: 日記[にっき]を{書[か]いたら|cd-tara}どう？
en: How about keeping a diary?
why: A casual suggestion is 〜たらどう; the other forms cannot be followed by どう this way.

jp: 暑[あつ]いなら、エアコンを{つけたら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: If you're hot, why don't you turn on the air conditioner?
why: Suggesting an action to the listener is 〜たらどうですか; the other forms do not form a suggestion.

jp: この薬[くすり]を{飲[の]んでみたら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: Why don't you try taking this medicine?
why: Advice to try something is 〜てみたらどうですか; the other forms cannot make a suggestion.

jp: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]く{寝[ね]たら|cd-tara}どう？
en: Why don't you go to bed early today?
why: A friendly suggestion is formed with 〜たらどう; the other forms cannot be followed by どう.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]少[すこ]し{運動[うんどう]したら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: Why don't you exercise a little every day?
d: 運動[うんどう]するので
why: A recommendation to the listener is 〜たらどうですか; the other forms do not suggest anything.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]が{遅[おく]れたら|cd-tara}、先[さき]に始[はじ]めていてください。
en: If my train is late, please start without me.
why: A request about what to do if something happens takes たら; と cannot lead into a request and ので would state the delay as a fact.

jp: 駅[えき]で{会[あ]ったら|cd-tara}、一緒[いっしょ]に行[い]きましょう。
en: If we run into each other at the station, let's go together.
why: A proposal that follows a chance meeting takes たら; と cannot lead into 'let's' and ので would treat the meeting as already arranged.
